findings.summary: The queries page ends with a flow diagram of serial mutation execution, three blocks before mutations are introduced at all.

findings.summary: Page 4 opens with a cheat-sheet code block teaching alias and directive syntax, both of which are defined many pages later.
findings.evidence: First block of page 4: "key: field(args)          # alias", "field @include(if: $flag) # directive", "field @skip(if: $flag)    # inverse" — aliases are first explained on page 12 ("smallPic: avatar(size: 32) … # key = alias"), directives and `$` variables on pages 7–8.
findings.fix: Delete this block from page 4 and fold the two lines into the pages that own them: the alias line next to the `smallPic:`/`bigPic:` example on page 12, the `@include`/`@skip` lines next to the `query Row($deep: Boolean = false)` example on page 8.

findings.summary: The "Non-null is contagious" callout states the consequence of `!` on page 4, but the table that defines what `!` means is on page 5.
findings.evidence: Page 4: "Non-null is contagious … One deep failure nulls an entire branch, sometimes all of `data`. Mark `!` only where a null is genuinely impossible." Page 5 (next page) is where "`String!` | null nullifies parent" and "`[Post!]!` | neither nullable" first appear; nothing before page 4 mentions `!`.
findings.fix: Move the "Nullability" heading and its `String` / `String!` / `[Post!]` / `[Post!]!` table from the top of page 5 to page 4, immediately before this callout, so the marker is defined before its failure mode is given.

findings.summary: The input-kind table misclassifies built-in scalars and enums: `Boolean` is listed under "Identity" and enums under "Composite".
findings.evidence: rows: ["Scalars","`Int` `Float` `String`"], ["Identity","`Boolean` `ID`"], ["Composite","enums, input objects"]
findings.fix: Relabel to match the spec's type kinds: put `Int Float String Boolean ID` under "Built-in scalars", enums under "Enums" (leaf types, not composite), and reserve "Input objects" for the composite input row.

findings.summary: An unlabeled flow diagram depicting serial mutation execution sits on the page that states sibling fields run in parallel, implying queries commit field-by-field.
findings.evidence: Page bullets: "Sibling fields execute in PARALLEL, reads are safe"; page's closing diagram nodes: ["parse","`a` runs","`a` commits","`b` runs","`b` sees `a`"]
findings.fix: Title the diagram "Mutation root: serial" (or move it to the "Top level runs serially" section on the Mutation Root page) so it is not read as the query execution model.

findings.summary: The serial-mutation example uses alias syntax as its labelling device seven pages before aliases are explained.
findings.evidence: Page 5: "mutation Two {", "  a: rename(id:\"1\") { id }", "  b: publish(id:\"1\") { status }" — the alias rule ("`alias: field` — the result lands under the alias key") is on page 13, and here the aliases are not even required, since `rename` and `publish` are different fields.
findings.fix: Drop the `a:`/`b:` prefixes in this example and refer to the fields by name in the trailing comment ("# publish runs after rename commits"), keeping alias syntax for page 12–13.

findings.summary: A bullet whose subject is the operation name says names belong only in scratch work, contradicting the deck's own argument for naming every shipped operation.
findings.evidence: Bullets after `query GetUserProfile`: "The name is pure metadata — no effect on response shape" / "No effect on execution semantics either" / "Fine in GraphiQL and scratch work, never in shipped code"
findings.fix: Name the real subject of the third bullet: "Anonymous operations: fine in GraphiQL and scratch work, never in shipped code".

findings.summary: The variable-coercion table claims an omitted non-null variable is always an error, ignoring that non-null variables may carry a default value.
findings.evidence: Table row: "omitted" | Nullable var: "default applies" | Non-null var: "error"
findings.fix: Change the non-null/omitted cell to "default, else error" (per CoerceVariableValues: if no value is supplied and a default exists, the default is used; the request error is raised only when there is no default or the value is null).

findings.summary: The `query Row` sample has an extra closing brace and is not parseable GraphQL.
findings.evidence: "    posts @include(if: $deep) { id } } }","}   # one doc, two shapes" — three selection sets are opened but four braces are closed.
findings.fix: Drop one brace, e.g. `query Row($deep: Boolean = false) {` / `  user { name` / `    posts @include(if: $deep) { id } } }` with no trailing `}` line, moving the `# one doc, two shapes` comment onto the last line.

findings.summary: The defence against alias fan-out abuse rests on "cost analysis", a mechanism the handbook never defines anywhere.
findings.evidence: Page 13: "Cost analysis counts every copy separately" and "Bound the fan-out … Aliased duplicates multiply resolver work" — no page introduces query complexity scoring or depth limiting (syllabus chapter 9 is not covered by these slides).
findings.fix: Add one line on page 13 defining the term at point of use, e.g. "Cost analysis = a per-field score summed before execution; requests over budget are rejected", so the defence is intelligible without chapter 9.
